source: Initial seed from Cowork session 2026-04-28. Sourced from Netflix Tudum, Tom's Guide, Rotten Tomatoes, Anime News Network, and Crunchyroll Spring 2026 simulcast announcements. Refresh weekly via the scheduled task.

hero.title: Widow's Bay
hero.about: Matthew Rhys (The Americans, Perry Mason) plays the mayor of a small New England town that may or may not be cursed. Created by Katie Dippold, who wrote The Heat and Spy and worked on Parks & Recreation. Apple is positioning it as a genre-bender — comedy + horror + thriller + character drama all in one show, the kind of premise where a town's quirks slowly turn sinister. Eight-episode first season, premieres April 29 with multiple episodes then weekly.
hero.why: Off-beat tone, supernatural premise, plot-twist machinery, ensemble acting — that's four of your top 4–5⭐ signals firing at once. And Dippold wrote two of your 'Loved' list films (The Heat, Spy) — same comic instincts, longer runway.

new_this_week.title: Stranger Things: Tales From '85
new_this_week.about: Animated anthology spin-off set in summer 1985, the year between Seasons 2 and 3 of the live-action series. Tells previously-unseen Hawkins adventures — different threats, side characters, and Upside Down lore the main show didn't have room for. Different tone from prestige live-action; closer to a Saturday-morning-cartoon-with-stakes feel.
new_this_week.why: Even as animation, it's the same world that gave you world-building, supernatural threats, and 80s-flavored escapism. Anthology format means you can sample one episode tonight without committing to a full arc.

new_this_week.title: Running Point S2
new_this_week.about: Mindy Kaling-produced comedy. Kate Hudson plays Isla Gordon, the newly-installed president of the fictional Los Angeles Waves NBA franchise — a chaotic woman-in-a-man's-world workplace comedy loosely inspired by Jeanie Buss running the Lakers. Returning for S2 with the team chasing a championship.
new_this_week.why: Light ensemble workplace comedy with quick jokes — sits in the 'fine but not your strongest combo' lane. Try one episode if you want low-stakes background watching.

new_this_week.title: BEEF S2
new_this_week.about: Emmy-sweeping anthology returns with a brand-new cast and story: Oscar Isaac, Carey Mulligan, Charles Melton, and Cailee Spaeny in a fresh tale of a slow-burn personal feud spiraling into something much darker. Same showrunner (Lee Sung Jin), same tonal DNA — escalating bad decisions, cringe humor, real emotional stakes underneath.
new_this_week.why: S1 was widely praised for exactly the things you reward — dark humor, plot escalation, ensemble acting — and the anthology reset means no S1 baggage. High match on paper.

new_this_week.title: Big Mistakes
new_this_week.about: Dan Levy (Schitt's Creek creator/star) writes and directs this dark comedy about a sibling pair who get blackmailed into the world of organized crime after stumbling into a misunderstanding they can't undo. Limited series.
new_this_week.why: Levy's voice is well-known and off-beat. Crime-comedy + sibling chemistry is a workable lane for you, but the Levy-doing-darker-tone is unproven — try the pilot and bail if it feels too earnest.

new_this_week.title: Man on Fire
new_this_week.about: TV adaptation of A.J. Quinnell's 1980 novel (and the Denzel Washington film). Yahya Abdul-Mateen II plays John Creasy, a burned-out former soldier hired as bodyguard to a young girl in Mexico City; when she's kidnapped, his protection job becomes a methodical revenge mission.
new_this_week.why: Strong action-thriller premise but lacks the off-beat humor or sci-fi/supernatural elements that drive your 4–5⭐ ratings. Worth it only if you specifically want action-thriller in the mix tonight.

new_this_week.title: Outcome
new_this_week.about: Topical satire from Jonah Hill (writer-director). Keanu Reeves stars as Reef Hawk, an A-list Hollywood star whose career is upended when he's blackmailed by an old video. Cameron Diaz and Matt Bomer play his closest friends Kyle and Xander; Jonah Hill plays his crisis-management lawyer Ira. The comedy comes from watching genuinely bad people try to clean up after themselves.
new_this_week.why: Dark humor + ensemble + a blackmail-plot setup that's basically engineered for plot twists — three bullseyes against your taste profile. Cast pedigree is real.

new_this_week.title: Margo's Got Money Troubles
new_this_week.about: Adapted from Rufi Thorpe's 2024 novel. Elle Fanning plays Margo, a college dropout and aspiring writer who falls into financial chaos and has to figure things out alongside her ex-Hooters waitress mother (Michelle Pfeiffer) and ex-pro-wrestler father (Nick Offerman). Nicole Kidman, Greg Kinnear, and Rico Nasty round out a stacked supporting cast.
new_this_week.why: Quirky family-dramedy with a stacked acting bench. Closer to a Sundance-y character piece than your usual sci-fi/supernatural lane, but the off-beat premise and acting could land. Try the pilot.

new_this_week.title: Criminal Record S2
new_this_week.about: British police procedural starring Cush Jumbo and Peter Capaldi as detectives on opposite sides of a cold case. S1 examined institutional racism and competing investigative styles in modern London policing. S2 picks up the fallout and pushes both characters into new moral territory.
new_this_week.why: Procedurals aren't your sweet spot, but Capaldi-versus-Jumbo is real prestige-tier acting and the show traffics in the slow-reveal twists you respond to. Solid 'try' if you want a tighter, more grown-up thriller than Slow Horses.

new_this_week.title: Your Friends & Neighbors S2
new_this_week.about: Jon Hamm plays Andrew 'Coop' Cooper, a recently-divorced hedge fund manager who quietly burgles his obscenely wealthy suburban neighbors to keep up appearances. S2 raises the stakes when a new neighbor played by James Marsden moves in and starts piecing together what Coop is actually doing. Created by Jonathan Tropper (Banshee, See).
new_this_week.why: Hamm doing morally-gray comedy is exactly the deadpan-with-stakes register you reward (think Slow Horses energy). Marsden as the threat is great casting. Plot-twist machinery is built into the premise.

new_this_week.title: Shrinking S3
new_this_week.about: Bill Lawrence (Ted Lasso, Scrubs) co-creation. Jason Segel plays Jimmy, a grieving therapist who breaks every rule by saying exactly what he thinks to his patients. Harrison Ford as his crusty mentor and Jessica Williams as a colleague anchor a tight ensemble. S3 deepens the fallout from S2's big shifts.
new_this_week.why: Sits squarely in your 'light(ish) tone with substance' zone — closer to Fleabag's emotional honesty than to your sci-fi favorites. Critics call S3 the strongest season yet.

new_this_week.title: The Boys S5 (Final)
new_this_week.about: Final season of the superhero satire. Premise: superheroes are real, owned by a corporation (Vought), and almost all of them are corrupt narcissists; The Boys are a black-ops crew who try to keep them in check. S5 closes out the war between Butcher's crew and Homelander, with two-episode premiere then weekly drops through the May 20 finale.
new_this_week.why: Sci-fi + dark comedy + plot twists is your trifecta, and 'final season' means real stakes and payoff. If you've never started, S5 isn't the entry point — but if you have, this is appointment viewing.

new_this_week.title: Kevin
new_this_week.about: Adult animated comedy from Aubrey Plaza and Joe Wengert (writer on Big Mouth). Plaza voices Kevin, a cat who gets abandoned at an animal shelter when his owners break up and is forced to fend for himself among a cast of other shelter animals. Half-hour episodes, cynical-but-sweet tone.
new_this_week.why: Adult animation + off-beat + 30-min episodes is your Solar Opposites / Rick and Morty wheelhouse. Plaza's deadpan as the lead is a strong signal.

new_this_week.title: House of the Spirits
new_this_week.about: Eight-episode adaptation of Isabel Allende's 1982 novel. Multi-generational family saga spanning roughly half a century in an unnamed conservative South American country (modeled on Allende's Chile), following three generations of women — Clara the clairvoyant, her daughter Blanca, and granddaughter Alba — through political upheaval, class struggle, and quiet magical realism.
new_this_week.why: Magical realism overlaps with your supernatural taste, but the family-saga drama register is closer to your 'sad drama' lower-priority lane. Try if you want something prestige and slower-paced.

new_this_week.title: Nippon Sangoku: The Three Nations of the Crimson Sun
new_this_week.about: Original anime set in a near-future Japan that has fractured into three rival states warring for supremacy after a national collapse. Mixes geopolitical intrigue with mecha and conspiracy elements. Premiered April 5 on Prime in the US.
new_this_week.why: Sci-fi + world building is your wavelength, but political-intrigue anime can be slow-paced — a known miss signal for you. Try the pilot before committing.

new_this_week.title: Dr. Stone: Science Future Pt 3
new_this_week.about: Continuing adaptation of Riichiro Inagaki's manga. Premise: humanity is mysteriously turned to stone by a flash of light; thousands of years later, prodigy student Senku Ishigami awakens and rebuilds civilization from scratch using science — every episode is essentially 'how do we invent X with sticks and rocks.' Pt 3 continues the global science quest.
new_this_week.why: Hits the same bench as Demon Slayer and One Punch Man — anime + sci-fi + world-building + escapism. The rebuild-civilization premise has unusually high replay value because it teaches as it goes.

new_this_week.title: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime S4
new_this_week.about: Fan-favorite isekai anime, S4. A Japanese salaryman dies and is reincarnated in a fantasy world as a slime monster with steadily-growing powers; he ends up founding and ruling a multi-species nation. Lots of political world-building, large ensemble.
new_this_week.why: World building is the hook — but isekai tends to be slow-paced and goofy in a way that sometimes lands and sometimes doesn't for you. Worth a try if you want something low-stakes.

new_this_week.title: Dorohedoro S2
new_this_week.about: Long-awaited return of the cult anime adapted from Q Hayashida's manga. In a grim, surreal world divided between humans and magic-users (Sorcerers), the lizard-headed Caiman tries to find the magic-user who transformed his head — while teaming up with his friend Nikaido. Tone is dark but absurd, gory but slapsticky, and visually unlike anything else.
new_this_week.why: Off-beat + supernatural + dark humor is your sweet spot, and Dorohedoro is the kind of show critics use 'singular' for. Returning fans rate S1 very high.

new_this_week.title: Haibara's Teenage New Game+
new_this_week.about: Adaptation of Kazuki Amamiya's light novel. Premise: socially anxious college senior Natsuki Haibara mysteriously wakes up seven years in the past, one month before high school. Armed with the knowledge of his original life, he sets out to do high school properly this time — joining the popular group, building friendships, getting closer to the girl he never approached. Slice-of-life with 'second chance' framing.
new_this_week.why: Slice-of-life isn't your strongest match (no sci-fi/supernatural threat, low plot-twist density), but the time-loop premise has appeal if you want something gentle. Probably a 3⭐ for you, not a 4.

new_this_week.title: The Classroom of a Black Cat and a Witch
new_this_week.about: Magic-academy fantasy. Witch apprentice Spica Virgo can't use magic at all and has neither money nor connections to find a mentor. A talking black cat appears with magic of his own — but he's really a cursed human and wants Spica to help break the spell. Their goals align: secret master-apprentice pact, comedy, slow-build mystery.
new_this_week.why: Supernatural + off-beat premise + magic-academy framing is a workable taste fit — but it could land too earnest/YA depending on the writing. Try the pilot.

critics.title: A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms
critics.about: HBO's adaptation of George R.R. Martin's Tales of Dunk and Egg novellas, set roughly 90 years before Game of Thrones. Follows Ser Duncan the Tall ('Dunk'), a hedge knight of humble origins, and his small, sharp squire 'Egg' (a young Targaryen prince in disguise) as they wander Westeros looking for tournaments, trouble, and honor. Lighter, smaller-scale, more buddy-road-trip than the main saga.
critics.why: RT calls it 'a welcome return to Westeros that works better in the buddy-comedy arena.' Fantasy world-building + light banter + character-driven — closer to Slow Horses than to GoT in tone, which is good news for your taste.

critics.title: The Pitt S2
critics.about: Real-time medical drama (each episode covers one hour of a single 15-hour ER shift in Pittsburgh) starring Noah Wyle as Dr. Robby, the senior attending. From ER producers John Wells and R. Scott Gemmill. Ensemble cast of residents, nurses, and patients; almost no music, lots of overlapping dialogue. S2 widely called the best new drama on TV right now.
critics.why: Medical-drama register sits in your lower-priority 'sad drama' lane, BUT critics rave about the craft, ensemble work, and how briskly it moves. Worth one episode to see if the format grabs you the way it has critics.

critics.title: How to Get to Heaven from Belfast
critics.about: Lisa McGee's (Derry Girls) follow-up. Three lifelong Belfast friends — Saoirse the chaotic TV writer, Robyn the stressed-out mother of three, Dara the dependable carer — travel to County Donegal when the estranged fourth member of their teenage friend group dies unexpectedly. What starts as paying respects becomes a chaotic quest to solve her suspicious death while keeping their own dark secret buried. Six-episode comedy mystery; 95% on Rotten Tomatoes.
critics.why: Bullseye fit. McGee's Derry Girls-honed Irish/British humor + a comedy-mystery format engineered for plot twists + ensemble of great character actors. This is the strongest taste-match in the whole briefing.
